# Results

See [Powerpoint](
https://docs.google.com/presentation/d/17gjZdGj7l0s94G3m_Iklbe6CF6hvUdZ-) presentation, results as of February 26, 2026.

The table of primary performance metrics, organized by management levers, is presented in Figure \@ref(fig:pf-primary).
A full table with ancillary performance metrics is provided in Figure \@ref(fig:pf).

Tradeoff figures which compare two outcomes on a set of axes across management scenarios can inform the decision-making space, i.e. identify important management levers that decisively determine outcomes over other levers. 

A panel of tradeoff figures comparing P_PNI_50 and P_1300_NS can identify scenarios where both the PNI and spawner objectives are likely to be met (if both performance metrics are greater than 50 percent).
Such scenarios are found in the upper right corner of the tradeoff figure.
The decision-making space, and the answers to the three management questions posed earlier, can be identified through Figure \@ref(fig:tradeoff1).
An accompanying tradeoff figure showing median PNI and spawner abundances are shown in Figure \@ref(fig:tradeoff2).

First, freshwater stewardship, i.e., increasing freshwater survival, makes it more likely to achieve PNI and spawner objectives.
When viewing the column of panels from left to right (corresponding to higher survival), the various modeling scenarios indicated in the coloured points shift to the upper right corner.

Second, comparison of results in the top half (top 2 rows) with the bottom half of Figure \@ref(fig:tradeoff1) informs the importance of mass marking to achieve the PNI objective.
In the top 2 rows, almost all modeling scenarios provided P_PNI50 scores of less than 50 percent, indicating PNI > 0.5 was unlikely to occur without mass marking except in the most optimistic case (no in-river fishery, high freshwater survival, and mark-selective terminal fishery).
Within the bottom 2 rows, coloured points indicate the pNOB target in the modeled projections and describes the impact of selective brood. The PNI objective is frequently achieved only with the high pNOB target (compare blue points vs. red points) with low to medium freshwater survival. Notably, the increase in pNOB target (and PNI50 probability) does come at a cost of slightly reducing the probability of obtaining 1300 spawners.

Third, the comparison of the first to second row and the third to fourth row facilitates evaluation of mark-selective marine terminal fishing. While mark-selective fishing improves the performance metrics, the impacts are more marginal compared to other management levers. The quadrants of modeling scenarios do not switch quadrants depending on whether fishing is mark-selective or not.
Similarly, the modeling scenarios frequently do not move between quadrants based on in-river exploitation rate (pNOB target is the more impactful lever where the results do change quadrants). As a result, the presence of the in-river fishery does not conflict with PNI and spawner objectives.

In general, the spawner objective was achieved in most scenarios in the simulations. Notably, the spawner objective was not met under the following conditions: low freshwater survival, high pNOB target (with massing marking) and non-selective terminal fishery. This combinations results in low spawner abundance (regardless of in-river exploitation) due to low survival of natural-origin fish, which in turn reduces brood availability for hatchery production.

(ref:fig-pf-primary) Panel of primary performance measures reporting outcomes at the end of the projection for various modeling scenarios and management options. Primary performance metrics directly identify ability to reach pre-stated decision-making objectives. Columns of panels differentiate freshwater survival (fs) while rows identify presence (MM) or absence (no MM) of mass-marking, and presence (MSF_T) or absence (no MSF_T) of mark-selective fishing in the terminal fishery. Within each table, cell rows identify in-river management option (in-river exploitation rate, IRER) and pNOB target, and cell columns identify the primary performance metric.

